about: Every kind of change: swaps with alternatives, locked options and their masks, a stacked idiom and a riff; garnish of each placement, with removals; drawl and a swear infix inside a swap's region (covers); a US word swapped.

request.text: Good grief, are you crazy? You're overreacting, you're stupid and all talk, and I'm extremely busy cleaning up after you. I'm starving, let's get something to eat at McDonald's. The faucet in my apartment is broken. Then they lost their tents and chairs. He is an idiot and a liar. Calm down and stop complaining. I am going to the store.

response.text: Strewth, are ya mad as a cut snake? Beats me. Yer carrying on like a pork chop, you're a stubby short of a six-pack'n a big-noter, and I'm flat chat, flat out cleaning up after ya, ya drongo. Fair dinkum, I'm starvin', with a belly growling like a mixer full of rocks, let's 'ave a feed at Macca's. Well, the tap in my bloody unit is bung. Stone the flamin' crows, then they lost their bloody tents and chairs, the whole kit 'n caboodle. So anyway, he's thick as two short planks and a liar. Now, 'ave a cup of tea, a Bex'n a bloody good lie-down'n stop whingeing, like a loose sheet of tin in the wind. Anyway, I'm going to the store. Streeeewth.

bung-broken.gloss: Broken, not working, crook ("the telly's gone bung", "a bung knee").

c-mind-you.gloss: Adds a qualifying afterthought ("Mind you, his brother turned up").
c-mind-you.notes: Shared with British English, and very natural in an Australian yarn. Best on a sentence that qualifies the one before it, so keep the weight low.

riffs.text: like a flat-pack in a cyclone

cactus.notes: Of machines and things ("the ute's cactus"), not tired people. Older-sounding; Macquarie's blog thinks it may be fading, but it is still widely understood.

carry-on-like-a-pork-chop.form: carry on like a pork chop
carry-on-like-a-pork-chop.gloss: Behave in a ridiculously overwrought way.

crikey.gloss: An exclamation of surprise or alarm.

cup-of-tea-bex-lie-down.form: have a cup of tea, a Bex and a good lie-down
cup-of-tea-bex-lie-down.gloss: Settle down, you're overwrought (Bex was a headache powder; the line is from a 1950s revue).

flat-chat.gloss: Going as hard as possible; very busy.

flat-out.gloss: Busy as can be, no let-up.

flat-out-lizard.form: flat out like a lizard drinking
flat-out-lizard.gloss: Extremely busy, like a lizard lapping water flat on its belly.

g-aside-dunno.gloss: A shrug, I've no idea (the narrator answering their own question).
g-aside-dunno.notes: General informal English, very common in Australia. Same slot as the existing "search me." and "beats me."

g-aside-search-me.gloss: I've no idea (after a rhetorical question).

g-tail-and-stuff.gloss: A vague "and the like" after a list.
g-tail-and-stuff.notes: General English, well documented in Australian corpus studies; it adds a casual rhythm rather than Aussie colour.

hungry-enough-to-eat-the-arse-out-of-a-d.form: hungry enough to eat the arse out of a low-flyin' duck

mad-as-a-gumtree.form: madder than a gumtree full of galahs
mad-as-a-gumtree.gloss: Utterly mad, like a tree of shrieking cockatoos.
variants: as mad as a gumtree full of galahs

mad-as-a-meat-axe.form: as mad as a meat axe

not-the-full-quid.notes: Aus/NZ; means not very bright or a bit odd. Predicative only ("he's not the full quid").

off-rocker.gloss: Crazy. Also British; common in Australia.

roos-top-paddock.form: {subj} {have} a kangaroo loose in {poss} top paddock
variants: {subj} {have} a few roos loose in {poss} top paddock

rooted.notes: "Root" is Australian slang for sex, so "rooted" (exhausted; broken) is impolite: vulgarity 2 is right. Never use "root" for US "root for (a team)"; Australians say "barrack for". "Get rooted" is a rude brush-off, a different sense.

snags-short-of-a-barbie.form: a few snags short of a barbie

stubby-short-of-a-six-pack.form: a stubby short of a six-pack

stuffed.gloss: Exhausted, broken, or full of food.

troppo.gloss: Crazy, as if from too long in the tropics.

unit.gloss: A flat; the usual Australian word for an apartment.
